Q: Simple PHP API example A:

Variable names should describe what the variable contains, and have a consistent syntax.

  • So, for me, $method is unclear, it is a $requestMethod or perhaps even $httpRequestMethod. Shorter isn't always better. Now I admit that, in such a short piece of code, it takes only a few seconds to look up what a variable actually contains, but it will be more difficult when the code exists out of thousands of lines.
  • As mentioned before (see below) $uri should be something like $requestPath or $httpRequestPath. Note that you seemed to have used that, because it's in your code. Clearly you haven't tested your code before you published it here.
  • The syntax of $Body doesn't match the syntax of the other variables. Shouldn't it be $body, or $requestBody, or even $httpRequestBody?
  • The getData(...) function is also very terse. "Get data" from what, how? A better name for such a function would be something like executeDbQuery(string $query). Most functions return stuff, so there's no real point to talk about that.

Yes, this is an acceptable way to build a small API. After all, an API is nothing more than some code that responds sensibly to calls.

As for handling routes and HTTP methods, a few switch () statements will work for now. In the future you might want to have a separate PHP file for each route and method. Then you could use the names of those routes and methods to select the appropriate PHP file.

Q: Salesforce Development with Flutter A:

No there is not full support for in flutter for salesforce development but you can still build integrations with some boundaries and restrictions. Salesforce core mobile system is mainly built for native ( ios/ android) and some hybrid frameworks like corva.There is not complete official flutter that is equivlent to salesforce mobile. This means no plug and CRM development in Flutter. But their is an Flutter plugin exists for MobilePush SDK (Marketing Cloud) that supports

  1. Push notifications

  2. User attributes & tags

  3. Engagement tracking

but this is only for engagement and marketing features not for CRM development.

Q: Why does npm install most of the time corrupted? A:

Common Root Causes

  • Corrupted npm cache

  • Broken node_modules

  • Mismatch between package.json and package-lock.json

  • Network interruptions (quite common with some ISPs / VPNs)

  • Antivirus blocking files

  • Outdated Node.js / npm versions

Quick Fix (Works in Most Cases)

Try removing existing dependencies and cleaning the cache:

rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json
npm cache clean --force
npm install

In most cases, running a fresh npm install after cleanup resolves the issue (works ~80% of the time).
